title: Student can later deny having submitted the assignment
description: Because the submission originates from the student, if the act of upload is not bound to the student's authenticated session with adequate evidence (for example, a reliable submission receipt or audit trail), the student may plausibly repudiate having submitted this specific file at this time.
assumptions: The portal may rely only on basic login state and may not provide strong proof of submission to both parties.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on general LINDDUN repudiation structure; exact subnode may differ in the canonical threat tree.

title: Submission metadata can link the student to a specific course activity
description: The data in transit includes student id, course, and submission timestamp alongside the uploaded work file. Even aside from file contents, this metadata can be used to link the student to a particular course enrollment and assignment event.
assumptions: The flow or observable metadata is accessible to network observers, intermediaries, logs, or monitoring components beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode is approximate; grounded in linkability via correlated identifiers and event metadata.

title: Submission traffic can identify the student
description: Student id and associated submission metadata transmitted on this flow can directly identify the student, and the work file itself may also contain identifying information. If exposed in transit or through transport-layer metadata, the student's identity becomes apparent.
assumptions: Transport protection, endpoint logging, or intermediary handling may be insufficient to prevent exposure of identifiers in transit.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate; applies generally to identifiability from direct identifiers on the flow.

title: Assignment submission reveals sensitive academic behavior
description: The fact that the student is logging in and submitting an assignment for a specific course at a specific time discloses personal information about academic participation, deadlines, and behavior. The uploaded file may also reveal additional personal content beyond what is necessary for transport.
assumptions: Observers or unnecessary intermediaries can access payload or metadata, or the system exposes more information than needed during transmission.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node is approximate; this is a disclosure threat based on payload and metadata exposure.

title: Portal may collect or retain more submission data than necessary
description: On receipt, the portal processes the work file, student id, course, and timestamp. If it stores the full file, detailed timestamps, or associated identifiers longer than necessary or uses them for secondary purposes, the destination causes unnecessary disclosure and privacy risk.
assumptions: The portal may retain submissions, logs, and metadata beyond the minimum needed for grading and academic records.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate; intended to capture disclosure/excessive retention at the destination.

title: Student may be unaware of how submission data will be used
description: After receiving the submission, the portal may process the file and metadata for grading, plagiarism detection, analytics, support, or retention without the student's clear understanding. This creates a lack of transparency about downstream use of the submitted personal data.
assumptions: Notices about processing, retention, sharing, or automated analysis are incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate; this is a generic unawareness/transparency threat at the destination.

title: Submission processing may exceed the student's expectations or consent
description: If the portal uses the uploaded assignment and metadata for purposes beyond assignment handling—such as plagiarism services, model training, analytics, or extended retention—without an appropriate legal basis or valid consent/notice, the destination creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Additional processing beyond core educational administration is possible and may require specific notice, policy basis, or consent depending on jurisdiction and context.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate and legal applicability depends on institutional context and jurisdiction.

title: Portal shares identified student data with downstream grading service
description: The portal forwards student id together with course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. This is processing and disclosure of identified data, enabling the downstream service to directly associate the request and submission with a specific student.
assumptions: Student id is a unique identifier for a student within the institution and is not pseudonymous from P2's perspective.

title: Data flow contains a unique student identifier in transit
description: The transmitted payload includes student id, which is a unique reference to the data subject. Anyone with access to the flow contents, logs, traces, or message metadata may identify the student associated with the submission or grading request.
assumptions: The student id is present on the flow and remains intelligible to intermediaries or operational telemetry unless specifically protected.

title: Submission and grading requests can link student activity across courses or assignments
description: Because the same student id is sent with course and file reference on each request, observations of this flow can be linked over time to build a per-student activity history, such as which courses they are active in and when they submit or request grading-related actions.
assumptions: The same student id is reused across multiple requests and can be observed in flow contents or related telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement; the retrieved context did not include a linking node.

title: Received request data may create evidence tying a student to a submission or grading action
description: On receipt, the assignment & grading service can store student id, course, file reference, requesting role, and timestamps as evidence that a particular student initiated or was associated with a submission or grading-related request. This may later reduce the student's ability to deny involvement in that action.
assumptions: P2 logs or persists request details with sufficient integrity and retention to be used as evidence.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nr tree-node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context described the threat type but did not provide a specific node id.

title: Assignment service learns student-course participation from routed requests
description: By receiving student id together with course and file reference, the destination can infer personal information such as which course a student is enrolled in, that they are submitting work, and potentially timing or status of their academic activity.
assumptions: Course identifiers and file references are meaningful to P2 and reveal academic context beyond what is strictly necessary for routing alone.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure node citation is based on best judgement; retrieved context did not include disclosure subnodes.

title: Downstream reuse of submission request data may exceed the student's expectations
description: The assignment & grading service receives a combination of identifiers and academic context that could be reused for analytics, profiling, monitoring, or secondary operational purposes beyond handling the immediate submission or grading request, creating a risk that processing is not transparent or expected by the student.
assumptions: P2 may use or retain the received data for purposes beyond immediate transaction handling, and those purposes are not fully communicated to students.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on actual transparency and purpose limitation controls at P2; tree-node citation is best judgement.

title: Sharing identified academic-request data with the grading service may lack adequate consent or legal basis
description: The portal sends student id, course, file reference, and role to another process. If this downstream sharing or any secondary use by the grading service is not covered by an appropriate legal basis, institutional policy, or valid consent where required, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Applicable policy or law requires a defined legal basis, purpose limitation, and possibly notice/consent for this sharing and subsequent processing.
uncertainty_note: This depends strongly on the deployment's governance context; exact Nc node citation is based on best judgement.

title: Excessive disclosure when storing assignment submission metadata
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for the storage purpose, P2 causes avoidable disclosure of personal data to the data store by sending more data than needed.
assumptions: Assumes at least some of the stored attributes could be minimized, pseudonymized, or separated for the storage purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for an explicit/minimization-related disclosure pattern; exact node numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Linkability via combined submission metadata in transit
description: The flow carries a stable student identifier together with course and submission time. Even without inspecting file contents, this combination can enable linking multiple submissions or related actions to the same student across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is stable across submissions or courses and that observers or recipients can correlate repeated occurrences.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; threat applicability is strong because the metadata set is inherently correlatable.

title: Identifiability from student identifier and contextual metadata in transit
description: The transmitted student id directly identifies, or makes readily identifiable, the student associated with the assignment. Course and submission time further strengthen identification of the individual behind the submission.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is directly identifying within the system or can be resolved by parties with ordinary system access.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; the identifiability conclusion depends on how the student id is used in this environment.

title: Unnecessary retention or broad storage of assignment personal data
description: On receipt, the assignment store may retain the assignment file and associated student metadata longer than necessary or in a form broader than needed for grading and audit purposes, creating avoidable disclosure risk through storage.
assumptions: Assumes retention limits, field minimization, or segregation are not strictly enforced at DS1.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for storage-side avoidable disclosure/retention; exact numbering may differ by methodology version.

title: Linkability of student activity within the assignment store
description: By storing assignment content together with student id, course, and submission time, DS1 enables correlation of multiple submissions and academic activities belonging to the same student, potentially beyond what is necessary for the immediate purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 stores records in a way that permits querying or correlating by student id or related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; threat depends on DS1's indexing and access patterns.

title: Identification of the student from stored submission records
description: The stored record contains student id and contextual metadata that allow DS1 users or connected components to identify the student behind a submission record.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 is accessible to components or personnel able to resolve the student id.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; applicability is strong if student id is directly resolvable.

title: Storage without adequate notice or consent expectations
description: If students are not adequately informed that their assignment file, student id, course, and precise submission time will be stored in DS1, or if this storage exceeds the originally communicated purpose, the receipt and storage at DS1 may violate consent and transparency expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on notice/consent or purpose communication for this processing activity.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the legal basis and transparency model; exact tree-node id is approximate.

title: Teacher submits identified account credentials and role context
description: When logging in and requesting the review queue, the teacher provides identified data such as username/email and implicitly their teacher role or course affiliation. The act of sharing this identified data enables the portal to single out and recognize the teacher.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes account identifiers or equivalent authenticated session initiation data tied to a specific teacher account.

title: Teacher identity may be exposed in transit via request metadata
description: The request flow can carry identifying data in transit, such as account identifiers, session tokens, IP address, or course-specific request parameters, allowing the teacher to be identified from the communication itself.
assumptions: Assumes network-visible metadata or payload elements are available to intermediaries or logs.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is approximate because the retrieved context only explicitly mentions I.1.1 at a general level, not specifically transit metadata.

title: Portal processes identified teacher data to serve the submissions queue
description: The web app receives and processes identified teacher data to authenticate the teacher and determine which course submission queue to return. This is processing of identified data at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the portal maps the request to a specific teacher account and associated courses.

title: Teacher activity can be linked across requests through persistent identifiers
description: Repeated queue-request messages may contain stable identifiers such as session cookies, account IDs, device fingerprints, or consistent network metadata, enabling multiple actions by the same teacher to be linked together.
assumptions: Assumes persistent identifiers or stable metadata are present on this flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may vary; using a general linkability node because the provided context did not include the detailed L threat tree.

title: Portal can link teacher review activity across sessions
description: By storing account identifiers, session history, and course-access logs, the portal can link multiple login and queue-access events to the same teacher over time, building a profile of review behavior.
assumptions: Assumes the portal retains authentication and access logs tied to teacher accounts.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node is approximate due to missing detailed threat-tree context for Linkability.

title: Portal learns the teacher's interest in specific course review queues
description: The destination can detect that this teacher is currently accessing the grading/review queue for particular courses, revealing behavioral information about their work activity and timing.
assumptions: Assumes the request identifies or implies one or more courses whose submission queue is being requested.
uncertainty_note: Detailed detectability/disclosure sub-node is approximate because the retrieved context did not include D threat-tree details.

title: Insufficient transparency about logging and secondary use of teacher access requests
description: If the portal does not clearly inform teachers that login and queue-request events are logged, analyzed, or retained for purposes beyond immediate service delivery, the processing may be insufficiently transparent.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-context explanations are absent or incomplete for this request flow.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the actual notice presented to teachers; exact U sub-node is approximate.

title: Teacher may not have meaningful choice over processing needed to access the portal
description: To review submissions, the teacher may be forced to provide identified login and activity data to the portal without a practical alternative, which can undermine meaningful consent or user control over this processing.
assumptions: Assumes this processing is framed as consent-based or that user control is relevant in this context; if processing is instead strictly necessary under another legal basis, this threat may be less applicable.
uncertainty_note: This is context-dependent because employee/teacher portal access is often not based on freely given consent.

title: Excessive disclosure of student submission data to the teacher
description: The portal shares identifiable student names, work content, and submission times with the teacher. If the teacher does not need all of these attributes for the intended task, the process discloses more personal data than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes role-based access or data minimization may be insufficient, e.g. teachers can view submissions beyond their classes or more metadata than needed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Identification of students from data in transit
description: The flow contains direct identifiers such as student names alongside submission content and timestamps. Anyone able to observe the transmission could identify individual students.
assumptions: Assumes the transmission channel or endpoint display path could be observed by unauthorized parties if protections are weak.
uncertainty_note: Applies primarily if transport/session protections are inadequate; exact tree node id is approximate.

title: Linkability of student activity across submissions
description: Student names combined with work content and submission times can allow records from multiple submissions or sessions to be linked to the same student, revealing patterns of behavior or performance over time.
assumptions: Assumes repeated observations of this flow or associated metadata are possible.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is approximate due to missing detailed node mapping in context.

title: Secondary use or onward disclosure by the teacher
description: Once received, the teacher may process, copy, export, or share student submissions and timestamps beyond the original educational purpose, causing an additional disclosure threat at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes limited technical or organizational controls on teacher handling of displayed submissions.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine destination-side privacy risk, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id is chosen by best judgement.

title: Teacher may be unaware of privacy obligations when viewing student data
description: The destination party may not be sufficiently informed about permitted uses, retention expectations, or confidentiality obligations for the displayed student submissions, increasing the risk of privacy-invasive handling.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not clearly communicate privacy constraints or usage expectations to teachers.
uncertainty_note: Included as an unawareness threat at the recipient side; exact node id is approximate.

title: Teacher can later deny having submitted or authored a grade/feedback entry
description: Because the flow carries a grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id from the teacher to the portal, insufficient binding of the submission to the teacher's authenticated action could allow the teacher to plausibly deny having entered or changed the grade or feedback.
assumptions: Applies if the submission is not strongly tied to an authenticated session, timestamp, and tamper-evident audit trail.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement; exact sub-node may differ in the project's LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Teacher and student may be identifiable from data in transit
description: The transmitted payload contains direct identifiers or strong identifiers such as student id and grader id, and may also include contextual information in feedback text. If the flow is observable in transit, these data can identify the teacher and the student associated with the assignment.
assumptions: Applies especially if transport protection is absent, weak, or terminated in an untrusted environment.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may vary depending on whether the methodology distinguishes direct vs indirect identifiability.

title: Grade submissions can be linked across events or systems
description: Repeated transmissions containing stable student and grader identifiers enable linking multiple grading events to the same teacher and student over time. Even metadata about the submission timing and endpoints may support linking patterns of grading activity.
assumptions: Applies if identifiers are stable across submissions or if network/application metadata are retained and correlated.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; linkage may be driven by payload identifiers and/or communication metadata.

title: Sensitive academic evaluation data may be disclosed in transit
description: The flow contains confidential educational information: grade, qualitative feedback, and identifiers. Interception or unintended exposure during transmission would disclose personal data about the student's performance and the teacher's assessment.
assumptions: Applies if encryption, endpoint validation, or secure channel protections are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may differ depending on whether disclosure is framed as content disclosure or communication disclosure.

title: Portal may collect or retain more grading data than necessary
description: On receipt, the web app may store full feedback text, stable grader identifiers, timestamps, and related metadata longer than necessary or use them for secondary purposes beyond recording the assignment grade. This can violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention expectations.
assumptions: Applies if the portal lacks clear purpose limitation, minimization, or retention controls for grading records and associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed non-compliance subtree.

title: Portal may process grading data without sufficient transparency to teachers or students
description: After receiving the submission, the portal may not adequately inform teachers and students how grades, feedback, grader identifiers, and related metadata are stored, who can access them, how long they are retained, or whether they are reused for analytics or monitoring. This creates a lack of awareness about privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Applies if privacy notices, in-context explanations, or role-specific transparency mechanisms are missing or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; exact sub-node depends on the project's unawareness taxonomy.

title: Student identity is disclosed to the grade records database
description: The grading service writes a grade record containing student id together with course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. By sending a directly identifying student identifier, the source discloses the student's identity to the receiving datastore context.
assumptions: Assumes student id is directly identifying within the system and that DS2 is operated or administered by parties beyond the minimum set already entitled to know the student's identity.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Grade records can be linked across courses and assessments via student id
description: By writing persistent records keyed by student id, the grading service enables linkage of multiple grade entries for the same student across courses, assignments, and time. This can reveal academic performance patterns beyond a single grading event.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 stores multiple records over time and uses student id or equivalent stable key that permits correlation.
uncertainty_note: Threat is grounded in the stable student identifier included in the flow; exact tree node id is approximate.

title: Grader activities can be linked over time via grader id and timestamp
description: Including grader id and timestamp in each written grade record allows the recipient context to correlate grading actions by the same grader across courses and periods, potentially exposing workload, behavior, or decision patterns.

uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate.

uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate because detailed datastore-oriented disclosure nodes were not provided.

title: Grade records may be stored or reused beyond the student's reasonable expectations
description: The destination database may retain grade records, feedback, grader identifiers, and timestamps for longer periods or for secondary uses such as analytics, ranking, or staff monitoring, which may exceed what students and graders reasonably expect from the grading transaction.
assumptions: Assumes retention periods, secondary uses, or internal analytics are not fully aligned with the original grading purpose or are not clearly communicated.

title: Storage of detailed grade records may violate data minimization or retention obligations

If all fields are not necessary for the stated purpose, or if they are retained longer than permitted, the processing may fail to comply with privacy obligations such as minimization, purpose limitation, or retention control.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policy or legal requirements constrain which fields may be stored and for how long.
uncertainty_note: Compliance assessment depends on jurisdiction and institutional policy; exact tree node id is approximate.

title: Student provides identified request data
description: To request grades and feedback, the student typically sends identified data such as login credentials, student number, session identifiers, or other account-linked request parameters. The act of sharing this identified data makes the student identifiable to the portal.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal requires authenticated or otherwise account-linked requests rather than fully anonymous access.

assumptions: Assumes normal web-app request metadata is present and observable to relevant parties on the communication path or intermediary infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is approximate because the retrieved context only explicitly provided I.1.1, which is broader than in-transit metadata identification.

title: Portal processes identified grade-request data
description: On receipt of the request, the grades portal processes identified data to determine which student's grades and feedback to retrieve. This makes the student identifiable within the receiving process.
assumptions: Assumes the portal authenticates the requester and maps the request to a specific student record.

title: Repeated grade requests may be linkable over time
description: Multiple requests on this flow can likely be linked to the same student through stable identifiers such as session cookies, account IDs, device fingerprints, or network metadata. This enables correlation of the student's access patterns over time.

uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node citation is based on best judgement; the retrieved context did not include a specific linkability node.

title: Portal can link grade-access events to the same student
description: The receiving portal can correlate repeated requests for grades and feedback with the same identified student account, building a history of when and how often the student accesses academic results.

title: Portal learns the student's interest in specific academic results
description: By receiving the request, the portal can detect that the student is seeking their grades and feedback at a particular time, revealing behavior and potentially sensitive academic concerns or milestones.
assumptions: Assumes access events are observable or retained by the portal beyond transient routing.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is based on best judgement; no detectability node was included in the retrieved context.

title: Portal may disclose grades and feedback to the wrong student account
description: If the web app retrieves or renders records for an incorrect authenticated session, or fails to enforce object-level authorization, the process can send one student's grades and teacher feedback to another student. assumptions: Assumes the portal uses account-based access and that authorization/session binding defects are plausible for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement because the retrieved context only provided applicable threat types, not detailed node ids.

title: Grades and feedback could be intercepted in transit
description: If the portal displays grades and teacher feedback over an inadequately protected channel, an eavesdropper on the network path could read the student's academic results and comments while they are transmitted to the browser.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection could be absent, downgraded, or misconfigured on some deployments or endpoints.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for disclosure in transit was not included in the retrieved context.

title: Traffic metadata may reveal when a student checks grades
description: Even if content is encrypted, observable communication metadata such as timing, endpoint, message size, and access frequency can allow an observer to infer that a particular student is accessing the grades portal, potentially linking the student to grade-release events or academic review activity.
assumptions: Assumes a network observer or intermediary can see metadata about portal access.
uncertainty_note: Applies at the flow level via metadata; tree node id is best-judgement.

title: Displayed grades and feedback may be exposed on the student's device or surroundings
description: Once received, the information may be visible to other people using the same device, through shoulder surfing, shared browser profiles, notifications, screenshots, or cached pages. The privacy harm arises at the recipient side after receipt of the data.
assumptions: Assumes the student may use shared or unmanaged devices, or be in a non-private environment.

title: Repeated portal access patterns may enable linkage of parent and child identities
description: Even if content access is authorized, metadata on this flow—such as account identifiers, URLs, session identifiers, timestamps, and repeated access to a specific student's records—can help link a particular parent to a particular child and their school activity.

description: Displaying grades and submission history to the parent inherently reveals that the parent is associated with a specific child and school context. Observable metadata or content on the flow can identify the student and infer the parent-child relationship.

title: Parents may be unaware of secondary uses or monitoring associated with viewing the child's records
description: While presenting grades and submission history, the portal may also collect analytics, access logs, or behavioral data about the parent's viewing activity without making these uses understandable. This creates unawareness about how personal data related to the viewing interaction is processed.
assumptions: Assumes the portal logs or analyzes parent access behavior and does not fully explain this to users.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on whether such monitoring or secondary processing actually occurs.

description: Because this flow carries high-impact administrative actions affecting user accounts and family relationships, insufficient binding of the action to the administrator's identity can let the administrator later repudiate having performed the change. This undermines accountability for privacy-relevant changes to names, emails, roles, and relationships.
assumptions: Applies if the portal does not strongly authenticate the administrator session or does not create tamper-evident audit records for account-management actions.

title: Administrative account-management traffic can identify affected individuals and families in transit
description: The payload contains names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. If the flow is observable in transit, these attributes can directly identify students, parents, and administrators, and reveal which accounts or family links are being managed.
assumptions: Applies if transport protection is absent, weak, terminated in an untrusted segment, or if intermediary logs/monitoring expose request contents or URLs.

title: Relationship-management data in transit can link parents to children and administrators to specific families
description: This flow explicitly carries parent-child links and account-management operations. Observation of the traffic or its metadata can enable linking a parent to a child, correlating multiple family members to one household, or associating a particular administrator with specific students or families.
assumptions: Applies if message contents or metadata are visible to network observers, intermediaries, or shared logging systems.

title: The portal can learn more than necessary about family relationships and account attributes
description: On receipt, the web app processes names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. If it collects or retains more attributes than needed for the administrative task, or exposes them broadly within the application, the destination learns and processes excessive personal data about students, parents, and staff.
assumptions: Applies if the portal lacks data minimization, purpose limitation, or role-based restrictions on which fields are accepted and processed for each admin action.

title: The portal may disclose account and family-link data to unauthorized parties after receipt
description: Once received, the portal stores or processes names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. Weak authorization, insecure storage, verbose logs, or overly broad admin interfaces can disclose these data to unauthorized staff, other users, or third parties.
assumptions: Applies if access control, tenant/school scoping, logging hygiene, or storage protections are insufficient.

title: The portal may use administrative relationship data for secondary purposes without user awareness
description: Data submitted to create or manage accounts and parent-child links could be reused by the portal for analytics, profiling, support, or other secondary purposes beyond account administration. Such reuse can occur without the affected parents, children, or staff understanding how their relationship data are used.
assumptions: Applies if privacy notices are incomplete, consent/legal basis is unclear for secondary uses, or internal reuse is not purpose-limited.

title: Affected users may not be adequately informed or given control over account and relationship changes
description: The portal receives and acts on changes to accounts and parent-child links that materially affect parents and children. If the system does not provide appropriate notices, review mechanisms, or means to correct erroneous links and account attributes, affected individuals may lack awareness and control over processing of their personal data.
assumptions: Applies if the system does not notify affected users of changes, lacks correction workflows, or does not surface privacy-relevant consequences of admin actions.

title: Grading service can link students to parents when writing relationship records
description: By writing parent-child relationship links together with account records, the Assignment & Grading Service creates an explicit association between identities that enables linkage of a student account to a parent/guardian account.

title: Account directory becomes a central source for linking family and account identities
description: Once the directory stores account records and parent-child links, it can correlate multiple records over time and across services, making it possible to link children, parents, and related account attributes within one repository.

description: The act of sending parent-child relationship links and account records reveals identifying information and family associations from the grading service to another component, increasing identifiability of the involved data subjects.

title: Account and relationship data in transit may identify parent and child
description: The data flow itself carries account records and parent-child links. If observed in transit, these contents can directly identify individuals or make them identifiable through combinations of attributes and relationship metadata.

title: Stored relationship links may reveal sensitive family details

description: After receiving account records and parent-child links, the directory could process or expose them for secondary purposes such as broader profiling, access decisions, or cross-service synchronization not expected by the data subjects.

description: If data subjects or guardians were not adequately informed that grading-derived account records and family relationship links would be stored in the account directory, the processing may violate consent, notice, or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: The system relies on consent, notice, or similar transparency obligations for this processing, and these may not explicitly cover directory storage of relationship links.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and governance model; exact subtree is approximate.

title: Excessive disclosure in full backup replication to third-party host
description: The Assignment & Grading Service sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third-party cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup/replication. title: Recipient-side overexposure and secondary access to replicated student data
description: Once received by the cloud hosting provider, the replicated backup may be accessible to provider personnel, subprocessors, or management tooling beyond what is necessary to deliver the service. This creates avoidable disclosure of grades, assignments, and directory data at the destination.

title: Identifiability from replicated account directory and grade records in transit
description: The backup flow contains directly identifying account-directory information together with grade records and assignments. If the flow is observed or insufficiently protected in transit, individuals can be directly identified from the transmitted dataset.

title: Linkability of academic performance with account identities during transfer
description: Because the same backup shipment includes account-directory data, assignments, and grade records, the flow enables linking a student's identity to their coursework and performance. Even if some fields were pseudonymous in isolation, the combined transfer makes correlation straightforward.
assumptions: Assumes the replicated datasets share common identifiers or can be joined by account keys.

title: Excessive disclosure from grade records database
description: The grade records database may disclose more personal data than necessary when serving the grading service, e.g. full grade histories or records for multiple roles (student, parent, teacher) when only a subset is needed for the requested view. Because grade records are highly sensitive educational data, overbroad reads increase privacy exposure.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 can return broader record sets or attributes than strictly needed for each view-building operation.

title: Identifiability of students and related parties in transit
description: The flow likely carries directly identifying educational records or stable identifiers that allow the grading service to identify specific students, parents, and teachers. Even if the service is authorized, the data flow itself contains identifying content whose exposure would reveal data subjects’ identities.

description: Because the grading service reads grade records to build multiple role-specific views, the transferred records may contain stable identifiers or relationship keys that enable linking a student’s grades with parent accounts and teacher assignments.
